detailed_description: The Byte Counter shows how many bytes a piece of text takes up in the browser. Paste or type text into the textarea and the tool reactively reports the character count, the UTF-8 byte count from the browser's TextEncoder, an approximate UTF-16 byte count using two bytes per JavaScript code unit, the ASCII byte count using one byte per code unit, the line count, and the UTF-8 size rendered in bytes or kilobytes. It does not provide encoding dropdowns, hex dumps, copy/reset buttons, surrogate-pair analysis, file uploads, or downloads.
usage_steps: Type or paste text into the input textarea
Read the character count card for the JavaScript string length
Read the UTF-8 bytes card computed with the browser's TextEncoder
Read the UTF-16 bytes card, which assumes two bytes per JavaScript code unit
Read the ASCII bytes card, which assumes one byte per code unit
Read the line count and the UTF-8 size card that switches to KB above 1024 bytes
usage_examples: Check how many UTF-8 bytes a short tweet or meta description will take
Compare UTF-8 and approximate UTF-16 byte counts for the same string while writing notes about encodings
Estimate whether a configuration value fits a small text field by reading the UTF-8 size in bytes or KB
Quickly count characters and lines of pasted text without opening another editor

faqs.question: Is the Byte Counter free to use?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Byte Counter is completely free with no signup or login, and every feature is available without limits.

faqs.question: Is my text safe when I use this tool?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. All counting runs locally in your browser with the built-in TextEncoder, so your text is never uploaded to any server.

faqs.question: Do I need to install anything?
faqs.answer: No. The Byte Counter is a browser-based tool — open the page and start typing, with no software or plugins required.

faqs.question: Why are the UTF-8 and UTF-16 byte counts different?
faqs.answer: UTF-8 uses one byte for ASCII characters but two to four bytes for accented letters, CJK text and emoji. The UTF-16 card is an approximation that assumes two bytes per JavaScript code unit, which is why the two counts usually differ for non-ASCII text.

faqs.question: How fast is the counting?
faqs.answer: Counting happens reactively in your browser as you type, typically finishing within milliseconds even for large texts.
